Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Naml (The Ant), because the word (al-naml) is unique to it in the Noble Qur'an, and because it includes the story of the ant that the Prophet of Allah, Sulayman (peace be upon him), passed by in the Valley of the Ants, along with his account concerning it and the wisdoms it contains.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Glorifying the status of the Qur'an, bestowing favour upon the Prophet ﷺ through it, and that it is guidance for whoever Allah makes it easy for him to be guided by it; and the challenge (to produce its like) through knowledge of what it contains of the reports of earlier peoples.

• Manifesting the blessing of Allah upon the noble Prophet Sulayman through prophethood, kingship, and the subjugation of the jinn and the birds, his giving thanks for it, his calling to Allah with wisdom and far-sighted insight, and clarifying the fundamentals of belief to which every messenger calls.

• Mentioning the proofs and evidences of the Oneness and existence of Allah from His signs and creatures, and disputing with the polytheists about the falsehood of their religion and the falsity of their deities.

• Affirming the Resurrection, and mentioning some of the terrors and scenes that the wrongdoers will see on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be terrified and agitated, and come to their Lord humbled; and reminding those who deny the Resurrection of the fate of their predecessors who denied (the messengers).

[The Tafsir]

﴿Ṭā-Sīn﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah. ﴿These are the verses of the Qur'an﴾, and they are the verses of the Mighty Book, clear in meaning and evident in indication, with what it contains of knowledge, wisdoms and laws. So the Qur'an is the Book, and Allah has combined the two names for it.

These are verses that guide to the path of success in this world and the Hereafter, and that give good tidings of excellent reward to the believers who affirmed them and followed their guidance: those who establish the five prayers with all their pillars complete and their conditions fulfilled, who give the obligatory zakat (zakah) to its rightful recipients, and who have certainty in the Hereafter and what it contains of reward and punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 4–5:

Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made their evil deeds appear attractive to them, so they see them as good; and they wander bewildered in them. Those are the ones for whom is the evil torment in this world—killing, captivity, humiliation and defeat—and in the Hereafter they are the greatest of people in loss.

And indeed you, O Messenger, are receiving the Qur'an from Allah, the All-Wise in His creation and His management, who has encompassed everything in knowledge.

Recall the story of Musa (Moses) when he said to his family, as he traveled from Madyan (Midian) to Egypt: "Indeed, I have seen a fire. I will bring you news from it that will guide us to the way, or I will bring you a burning brand from it, so that you may warm yourselves by it against the cold."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 8–12:

When he came to the fire, Allah called out to him and informed him that this place had been sanctified and blessed by Allah, and so He made it a place for speaking to Musa and sending him. And [He informed him] that Allah blessed those within the fire and those around it from among the angels, and [this is] an exaltation of Allah, Lord of the creation, above whatever is not befitting to Him. "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the One deserving of worship alone, the Mighty, the Victorious in My retribution against My enemies, the Wise in the management of My creation." ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So he threw it down, and it became a serpent. When he saw it moving with the agility of a swift serpent, he turned and fled and did not return to it. So Allah reassured him with His saying: ﴿O Musa, do not fear. Indeed, those whom I have sent as messengers do not fear in My presence. But whoever transgresses the limit through a sin, then repents, replacing the goodness of repentance after the ugliness of sin, indeed I am Forgiving toward him and Merciful to him.﴾ So no one should despair of the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. ﴿And insert your hand into your garment at the opening of your chest; it will come out white, without disease, among nine signs.﴾ These, along with the hand, are: the staff, the years of drought, the reduction of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and blood, to support you in your message to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a people who transgressed the command of Allah and disbelieved in Him.

So when these miracles came to them, clear and evident, by which whoever looked at them could see the truth of what they indicated, they said: "This is clear, evident magic."

Pharaoh and his people denied the nine clear signs, which were evident proofs of Moses' truthfulness in his prophethood and the truth of his call. They denied them with their tongues, claiming that they were not from God, although they were certain of them in their hearts, out of transgression against the truth and arrogance in refusing to acknowledge it. So look, O Messenger, at how the end of those who disbelieved in the signs of God turned out, those who spread corruption on earth, so God drowned them in the sea. In that is a lesson for whoever takes heed.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 15:

And We certainly gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they both said: "All praise is due to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants." And in the verse is evidence of the nobility of knowledge and the elevated standing of those who possess it.

Sulayman inherited (from) his father Dawud in prophethood, knowledge and kingship. Sulayman said to his people: "O people, we have been taught the speech of the birds and have been given understanding of it, and we have been given of everything that is needed. Indeed, this which Allah, the Exalted, has bestowed upon us is truly the clear favor that sets us apart above all others."

And Solomon's armies, of jinn, humans and birds, were gathered for him on the march. Despite their great numbers, they were not left unattended; rather, over each category there were those who would hold back the first of them until the last of them caught up, so that they would all stand together in good order.

Until, when they came upon the Valley of the Ants, an ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive." So he smiled, laughing at the words of this ant, because of her understanding and her guidance to warning the ants. He felt the blessing of God upon him, and turned to Him, supplicating: "My Lord, inspire me and enable me to be grateful for Your blessing with which You have blessed me and my parents, and to do righteous deeds that You are pleased with, and admit me by Your mercy into the bliss of Your Paradise among Your righteous servants whose deeds You have accepted."

He felt the blessing of God upon him, and turned to Him, supplicating: "My Lord, inspire me and enable me to be grateful for Your blessing with which You have blessed me and my parents, and to do righteous deeds that You are pleased with, and admit me by Your mercy into the bliss of Your Paradise among Your righteous servants whose deeds You have accepted."

And Solomon inspected the state of the birds that were subjected to him, and of those that were absent from him. He had among them a distinguished and well-known hoopoe, but he did not find it, so he said: ﴿Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is it that it is among the absent?﴾ Has something concealed it from me, or was it among those who are absent from me, so that I have not seen it because of its absence? Then, when it became clear that it was absent, he said: ﴿I will surely punish it with a severe punishment for its absence, as a discipline for it, or I will surely slaughter it as a penalty for what it did, since it failed in what it had been subjected to, or it must bring me a clear proof that contains an excuse for its absence.﴾

Then the hoopoe stayed away for a short while and came back. Sulayman rebuked him for his absence and his delay. The hoopoe said to him: "I have learned what you have not learned, understanding it fully and completely. I have come to you from the city of Saba' in Yemen with news of great importance, and I am certain of it."
I found a woman ruling over the people of Sheba, who has been given of everything, the means of worldly life, and she has a great throne on which she sits to manage her kingdom.

I found her and her people worshipping the sun, turning away from the worship of God. Satan made their evil deeds, which they were committing, seem good to them, and diverted them from faith in God and from His oneness. So they are not guided to God, to His oneness, or to worshipping Him alone.

The Shaytan (Satan) made their deeds appealing to them, so that they would not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden and concealed in the heavens and the earth, such as rain and plants and other things, and who knows what you conceal and what you disclose. Allah, there is no deity deserving worship except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne, for the Throne of the Most Merciful is the greatest of the created things.

The hoopoe left, delivered the letter to the queen, and she read it. She then gathered the nobles of her people and said to them: "There has come to me a letter of great worth, from a person of high standing."

Then she explained what it contained, saying: It is from Sulayman, and it begins with "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful," (not to be arrogant or haughty toward what I have called you to), and come to me in submission to Allah in His oneness and obedience, surrendering to Him.

She said: "O nobles, advise me in this matter. I would not decide any matter except in your presence and with your counsel."

They answered her: "We are people of strength in numbers and equipment, and people of valor and courage in the fierceness of war. But the matter is left to you, and you are the one of sound judgment. So consider what you will command us. We will hear your command and obey you."

She said, warning them against confronting Solomon with hostility and explaining to them the evil consequences of fighting: "Indeed, when kings enter a town with their armies by force and compulsion, they ruin it and make the most honored of its people the most humbled. This is their constant, established practice, so that people will fear them. And indeed, I am sending a gift to Solomon and his people, containing precious wealth, to appease him with it, and I will wait to see what the messengers return with."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 36:

When the envoy came to Sulayman with the gift, he said, disapproving of that and speaking of the blessings of Allah upon him: "Would you give me wealth to please me? What Allah has given me of prophethood, kingship and abundant wealth is better and more excellent than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in the gift that is presented to you, because you are a people of boasting in worldly things and of vying with one another in them."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 37:

Sulayman (peace be upon him) said to the messenger of the people of Sheba: "Return to them. By Allah, we will come to them with armies against which they have no power to resist or confront, and we will surely expel them from their land in humiliation, abased and disgraced, unless they submit to the religion of Allah alone and abandon the worship of anyone other than Him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 38:

Sulayman said, addressing those whom Allah had subjected to him from among the jinn and mankind: "Which of you will bring me her great throne before they come to me in submission and obedience?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 39:

A powerful, strong ʿIfrit (ʿIfrit) among the jinn (unseen beings) said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from this seat of yours, where you sit to judge between the people. Indeed, I am strong enough to carry it, and trustworthy regarding what is in it. I will bring it exactly as it is, without diminishing anything from it or changing it."

The one who had knowledge from the Book said: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." So when Sulayman saw it placed firmly before him, he said: "This is from the favour of my Lord, to test me: whether I will be grateful, or whether I will be ungrateful. Whoever is grateful, his gratitude benefits only himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is free of need, Most Generous."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 41:

Sulayman said to those around him: "Alter the throne of her kingdom on which she sits, into a form that she will not recognize when she sees it, so that we may see whether she will be guided to recognizing it, or whether she will be among those who are not guided."

When the Queen of Sheba came to Solomon in his assembly, she was asked: "Is your throne like this?" She said: "It is as if it were it." So it became clear to Solomon that she had answered correctly, and she had come to know the power of God and the truth of Solomon's prophethood, peace be upon him. Solomon said: "And we were given knowledge of God and of His power before her, and we were submissive to the command of God, following the religion of Islam."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 43:

What had prevented her from worshipping God alone was what she used to worship besides God, the Exalted. She was a disbeliever, had grown up among a disbelieving people, and had continued in their religion. Otherwise, she had enough intelligence and discernment to distinguish truth from falsehood, but false beliefs take away the insight of the heart.

It was said to her: "Enter the palace." Its courtyard was of glass, with water beneath it. When she saw the courtyard of the palace, she thought it was water whose waves were rippling, and she uncovered her shins to wade through the water. Sulayman said to her: "It is a smooth courtyard of clear glass, with water beneath it." Then she realized the greatness of Sulayman's kingdom, and said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself by what I was upon of shirk (association of partners with God), and I have submitted, following Sulayman, to the Lord of all the worlds."

We certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, saying: "Worship Allah alone, and do not associate with Him any other god." But when Salih came to them calling them to the Oneness of Allah and to worshipping Him alone, his people became two factions: one believing in him, and the other rejecting his call, and each of them claims that the truth is with them.

Salih said to the disbelieving group: "Why do you hasten to disbelief and to evil deeds, which bring upon you punishment, and delay faith and good deeds, which bring you reward? Why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah at once, and turn to Him in repentance, in the hope that you may be shown mercy?"

The people of Salih said to him: "We consider you and those with you, who have entered your religion, to be a bad omen." Salih said to them: "Your fortune, good or bad, is with Allah; it is He who decrees it for you and will recompense you for it. Rather, you are a people being tested with ease and hardship, good and evil."
And in the city of Salih—which is al-Hijr, located in the northwest of the Arabian Peninsula—there were nine men whose way was corruption on the earth, with nothing of righteousness mixed into it.

These nine said to one another: "Swear to one another by Allah that each of you will say to the others: 'We will surely come upon Salih suddenly at night and kill him and his family. Then we will say to the avenger of his blood from among his relatives: We did not witness their killing, and we are truthful in what we have said.'"

They plotted this scheme to destroy Salih and his family, a scheme of deception on their part. So We gave victory to our prophet Salih, peace be upon him, and We seized them with punishment while they were unaware, and they did not expect Our plot against them as a recompense for their plotting.
Look, O Messenger, with a lesson-seeking gaze at the outcome of the treachery of this group of men against their prophet Salih. We destroyed them and their entire people.

Then those are their dwellings, empty, with none of them remaining in them. God destroyed them because of their wronging themselves through polytheism and their denial of their prophet. Indeed, in that destruction and annihilation is a lesson for a people who know what We did to them, and this is Our custom regarding those who deny the messengers.
We saved Salih, peace be upon him, and the believers with him from the destruction that befell Thamud, those who used to guard themselves against God's punishment through their faith.

Mention Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you commit the deed of extreme ugliness, while you know its ugliness? Indeed, you come to men in their posteriors for lust instead of women? Rather, you are a people who are ignorant of the right of Allah over you, so you have opposed His command with that, and you have disobeyed His messenger with your ugly deed, which no one among the worlds had preceded you in."

Mention Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you commit the deed of extreme ugliness, while you know its ugliness? Indeed, you come to men in their posteriors for lust instead of women? Rather, you are a people who are ignorant of the right of Allah over you, so you have opposed His command with that, and you have disobeyed His messenger with your ugly deed, which no one among the worlds had preceded you in."

So the answer of Lot's people was only that some of them said to others: "Expel the family of Lot from your town. They are people who keep themselves pure from having intercourse with males." They said this to them mockingly.

So We saved Lot and his family from the punishment that was to befall the people of Lot, except his wife: We decreed that she would be among those left behind in the punishment, so that she would perish along with those who perished, because she used to help her people in their ugly deeds and was pleased with them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 58:

And We rained upon them a rain of stones of baked clay, which destroyed them. How evil was the rain of those who were warned, upon whom the proof had been established.

Say, [O Messenger]: "All praise and thanks are due to Allah, and peace from Him, and security upon His servants whom He has chosen for His message. Then ask the polytheists of your people: Is Allah, who possesses benefit and harm, better, or those whom they associate with Him, who possess for themselves and for others neither benefit nor harm?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 60:

And ask them: Who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water for you from the sky, and by it caused to grow gardens of pleasant appearance? It was not within your power to make their trees grow. Is there a god along with Allah who has done these deeds, that he should be worshipped alongside Him and associated with Him? Rather, these polytheists are a people who deviate from the path of truth and faith, and they make others equal to Allah in worship and veneration.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 61:

Is the worship of what you associate with your Lord better, or He who made the earth a place of stability, placed rivers within it, set firm mountains upon it, and placed between the two seas, the sweet and the salty, a barrier so that neither corrupts the other? Is there a deity worthy of worship alongside Allah who did this, that you should associate him with Him in your worship? Rather, most of these polytheists do not know the extent of Allah's greatness; so they associate others with Him out of blind imitation and wrongdoing.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 62:

Is it better (to worship) what you associate with Allah, or He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him, removes the evil that befalls him, and makes you successors (khulafa') to those who came before you on earth? Is there a god alongside Allah who bestows these favors upon you? Little do you remember and take heed, which is why you associate others with Allah in worship.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 63:

﴿Is it (better) to worship what you associate with Allah, or He who guides you through the darknesses of the land and the sea, and He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His mercy? Is there a god besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him!﴾

Translation of the commentary text:

The verse asks: Is worshipping what you associate with Allah better, or is He who guides you through the darknesses of the land and the sea, when you go astray and the paths become dark to you, and He who sends the winds as heralds of good news of His mercy, and of rain that gives life to dead land, better? Is there a deity worshipped besides Allah who does any of that for you, so that you call upon it instead of Him? Allah is exalted and sanctified above what they associate with Him besides Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 64:

Ask them: Who originates creation and then causes it to perish when He wills, and then brings it back? And who provides for you from the sky by sending down rain, and from the earth by causing crops and other things to grow? Is there any deity besides Allah who does that? Say: Bring your proof, if you are truthful in your claim that Allah, may He be exalted, has a partner in His dominion and in His worship.

Say, [O Messenger], to them: No one in the heavens or on the earth knows the unseen, except that which Allah has kept to Himself of knowledge, and they do not know when they will be raised from their graves at the establishment of the Hour. Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter will be complete [only] in the Hereafter, so they will be certain of the Last Abode and of the terrors within it when they witness them; yet in the world they were in doubt about it, and indeed their insight was blinded to it.

Say, [O Messenger], to them: No one in the heavens or on the earth knows the unseen, except that which Allah has kept to Himself of knowledge, and they do not know when they will be raised from their graves at the establishment of the Hour. Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter will be complete [only] in the Hereafter, so they will be certain of the Last Abode and of the terrors within it when they witness them; yet in the world they were in doubt about it, and indeed their insight was blinded to it.
The disbelievers who denied the oneness of God said: "Will we and our forefathers really be brought forth alive, as we are, after death, after we have become dust?"

We and our forefathers were indeed promised this resurrection before, but we have never seen any reality or occurrence of it. This promise is nothing but falsehoods which the ancients wrote down in their books and fabricated.

Say, [O Messenger], to these deniers: "Travel through the earth and look at the dwellings of those criminals who came before you. How was the end of those who denied the messengers?" God destroyed them because of their denial, and God will do to you the like of what He did to them if you do not believe.
Do not grieve over the polytheists' turning away from you and their denial of you, and do not let your chest be constricted by their scheming against you, for indeed God is your helper against them.
The disbelievers among your people say, O Messenger: "When will this promised punishment come, which you and your followers threaten us with, if you are truthful in what you threaten us with?"
Say to them, O Messenger: "Perhaps some of the punishment of Allah that you are asking to be hastened has already drawn near to you."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 73:

"And indeed your Lord is full of bounty towards mankind, by His leaving them without hastening punishment for their disobedience towards Him and their disbelief in Him. But most of them do not give thanks to Him for that, so that they would believe in Him and devote worship sincerely to Him."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, a concise Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 27, verse 74:

﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.﴾

And there is not a thing hidden from the sight of creatures in the heavens and the earth except that it is in a clear Record with Allah, and it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). That Record has encompassed everything that has occurred and everything that will occur.
Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel the truth concerning most of the matters over which they differed.
And indeed, this Qur'an is guidance from misguidance and mercy from punishment, for those who believe in it and are guided by its guidance.

Indeed, your Lord will judge between them concerning their differences, the Children of Israel and others, by His judgment regarding them. So He will take vengeance on the one who is in falsehood, and reward the one who does good. He is the Mighty (al-'Azeez), the Overpowering, so His judgment cannot be repelled, and the All-Knowing (al-'Aleem), so truth is never confused for Him with falsehood.
Therefore, O Messenger, rely upon Allah in all your affairs and place your trust in Him, for indeed He is sufficient for you. Surely you are upon the manifest truth, about which there is no doubt.

You, O Messenger, cannot make those hear the truth whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts, causing them to die (spiritually), nor can you make your call heard by those whom Allah has deafened from hearing the truth, when they turn their backs in aversion from you. For the deaf does not hear the call even when he is facing it; so how much more so when he turns away from it, fleeing and retreating?

And you, O Messenger, cannot guide out of error those whom Allah has blinded from guidance and right conduct. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses; they are the ones who submit and obey, responding to what you have called them to.

When the Word is fulfilled against them, because of their persistence in sins and transgression and their turning away from God's law and judgment, until they become among the worst of His creation, We will bring forth for them from the earth, at the end of time, a sign of the Major Signs of the Hour, which is "the Beast" (al-Dabbah), and it will speak to them that the people who denied the Resurrection were not believing in the Qur'an and in Muhammad (ﷺ) and his religion, and were not acting upon it.

On the Day when We gather from every nation a company of those who denied Our signs, their first ones will be held back until the last of them joins them, and then they will be driven on to the reckoning.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 84–85:

Until, when they arrive, He will say: "Did you deny My signs without grasping their knowledge, or what was it that you were doing?" And the word of punishment will be fulfilled against them because of their wrongdoing, and they will not be able to speak.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 86:

Have these deniers of Our signs not seen that We made the night for them to rest in and sleep, and the day to see by, so that they might strive for their livelihood? Indeed, in the alternation of the two is a sign for people who believe, affirming the perfect power of God, His oneness, and the great blessings He bestows.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 27, verse 87:

Remember, O Messenger, the Day when the angel will blow into the "Horn," and those in the heavens and those on the earth will be struck with terror, a great terror because of the awesomeness of the blast, except for those whom Allah excepts from among those He has honored and protected from terror. And all creatures will come to their Lord humbled and obedient.

You will see the mountains, thinking them fixed in place, yet they will pass by like the passing of clouds, driven along by the winds. This is the handiwork of God, who perfected everything He created. Indeed, God is well aware of what you do, O people, whether good or evil, and He will recompense you for it.

Whoever comes (on the Day of Resurrection) with the Oneness of Allah, faith in Him, worshipping Him alone, and righteous deeds, will have from Allah a great reward better and more excellent than them, namely Paradise; and they, on the Day of the Greatest Terror, will be secure.

Whoever comes with polytheism and evil, abominable deeds, their recompense will be that Allah casts them face-down into the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them as a rebuke: "Are you being repaid except for what you used to do in the world?"

Say, [O Messenger], to the people: "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city [Makkah], who has made it sacred and forbidden His creatures to shed blood unlawfully in it, to wrong anyone in it, to hunt its game, or to cut its trees. To Him belongs everything. I have been commanded to worship Him alone, to the exclusion of anyone else, and to be among those who submit to His command and hasten to obey Him, and to recite the Qur'an to the people. So whoever is guided by it and follows what I have brought, then the benefit of that and its reward belong only to himself. But whoever strays from the truth, say, [O Messenger]: 'I am only a warner to you of the punishment and retribution of Allah if you do not believe. I am but one of the messengers who warned their peoples, and guidance is not in my hand at all.'"

And say, [O Messenger]: "Praise belongs to Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them in yourselves and in the heavens and the earth, a recognition that guides you to the truth and makes clear to you falsehood. Your Lord is not unaware of what you do, and He will recompense you for that."
